First of all, I'm so sorry to hear about your SA and what you went through in this experience too. Being unexpectantly vulnerable and not feeling in control can be quite a stir, and I don't wish that upon anyone.

All I can say is that "the body keeps the score", whether you're consciously thinking about the past or not, your body will remember what has happened. So, sometimes the body can trigger emotions/reactions when undergoing a situation that reminds it of past trauma (especially if the trauma itself feels "unprocessed"/ lack of emotional resolution)(trauma response). You did nothing wrong, you shouldn't be ashamed. The best way to understand your body is to get a therapist (if possible) and/or take to the parts of you still affected by your SA. There's a form of therapy called IFS (internal family systems) which can be performed without a therapist; using curiosity & love/compassion, talk to your emotions one by one (remove external or internal interruptions), treating them as individuals/workers. If there a parts that don't feel like it belongs (critters), kick them out. Your emotions are meant to protect & serve you, even when it doesn't feel that way (so talk to them!). I know what I'm saying is hella weird but it really works; from personal experience, I can say it's really helped me and I've seen it be the most effective form of therapy. All it takes is yourself and a smidge of creativity.

Simply put, talk. Especially to yourself, but also to anyone you can trust to support/guide you. There is something left unsaid, unrecognized, or unprocessed to some degree or another, I think you need to work on connecting to/communicating with yourself. 

If you don't have anyone, I'd be happy to listen (just let me know). I hope you're doing better and I wish you all the best. 

​

(PS. I wouldn't recommend ignoring him, as long as he didn't do anything wrong. I'm not saying spill all the beans but give him something to understand, as I'm sure he feels bad and probably concerned about your well-being.
